successCriteria.description: The LeaveType string literal union exposes exactly the 6 values 'annual', 'sick', 'emergency', 'unpaid', 'maternity', 'paternity' — no more, no fewer — and a value outside this set is rejected by the TypeScript compiler.

The LeaveRequestStatus string literal union exposes exactly the 5 values 'DRAFT', 'SUBMITTED', 'APPROVED', 'REJECTED', 'CANCELLED' — no more, no fewer — and a value outside this set is rejected by the TypeScript compiler.

The LeavePolicy, LeaveRequest, and LeaveBalance interfaces are constructible as full objects; nullable fields accept null and optional fields accept undefined, and the compiler rejects objects missing required fields or assigning wrong types to constrained fields (e.g. leaveType must be a LeaveType, status must be a LeaveRequestStatus).

The CreateLeaveRequestDto and UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto interfaces are constructible; their optional fields (reason, rejectionReason) accept undefined, and the status field on UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto is constrained to LeaveRequestStatus.

The module barrel export re-exports all 7 public types (LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, LeavePolicy, LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, CreateLeaveRequestDto, UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto) so every type is importable from the module entry point.
Jest unit tests pass under the ts-jest preset, verifying the literal union value sets, object construction for each interface, and null/undefined handling for nullable and optional fields.
All type definitions compile cleanly under strict TypeScript (tsc --noEmit) with no implicit any and strict null checks enabled.

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json constraint rule no-any, severity high).
Strict TypeScript must be satisfied: no implicit any and strict null checks enabled (tsconfig.json strict: true).
Cross-module imports must go through the module's barrel index.ts only, never from internal files (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
This phase defines pure TypeScript types only — no database access, no runtime logic, no HTTP surface, no repository/service/controller code.
Tests must use the Jest + ts-jest preset and match the configured testMatch glob (**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)).
outOfScope: Repository, service, controller, and routes layers for the leave module (Phases 3, 6, 7, 8).
Leave state-machine transition logic and business rules (Phase 6/10) — this phase only defines the status union values, not the guards.
Policy enforcement logic (minimum notice days, auto-approval, manager-approval requirement) — Phase 10.
Shared error type classes (NotFoundError, ValidationError, etc.) — Phase 4.
Auth middleware and JWT utilities — Phase 5.
Database migrations and seed data — Phase 1 (already complete) and Phase 9.
Runtime validation (e.g. zod schemas) of DTO payloads at API boundaries — this phase defines static types only.

entityInvariants.invariant: The set of allowed leave categories is closed and finite: exactly annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity. No other string is assignable to the type.
The set of allowed lifecycle states is closed and finite: exactly DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. No other string is assignable to the type.
A policy's leaveType is constrained to the LeaveType union, ensuring a policy can only govern a recognized leave category.

A request's status is constrained to the LeaveRequestStatus union, and its reviewer/actor fields (approvedBy, rejectedBy, cancelledBy) and their timestamps are independently nullable, encoding that a request may be in a state where no reviewer has acted yet.
A balance is scoped to a single employee, leave type, and year, tracking entitlement, used, and accrued days as numeric values.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Barrel export of all leave domain types from the module entry point
interfaceConstraints.authRule: N/A — pure type module, no runtime auth
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Importing a non-exported name must fail at compile time; all 7 public types must be resolvable from the entry point.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Construction of each domain interface (LeavePolicy, LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, CreateLeaveRequestDto, UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto) as a typed object literal
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: The TypeScript compiler must reject object literals that omit required fields, assign a non-LeaveType to leaveType, assign a non-LeaveRequestStatus to status, or assign a non-null/non-undefined value to a nullable/optional field of incompatible type.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveType union values must exactly match the CHECK constraint on leave_policies.leave_type in migration 001: ('annual','sick','emergency','unpaid','maternity','paternity').
The LeaveRequestStatus union values must exactly match the CHECK constraint on leave_requests.status in migration 002: ('DRAFT','SUBMITTED','APPROVED','REJECTED','CANCELLED').

The LeaveBalance interface fields (entitlementDays, usedDays, accruedDays, year) must correspond to the leave_balances table columns (entitlement_days, used_days, accrued_days, year) defined in migration 003, preserving the unique scope of (employee_id, leave_type_id, year).
The barrel export pattern (re-export all public types from index.ts) must match the existing module convention used by src/modules/leave/index.ts and the module-structure rule in AGENTS.md.

integrationPoints.why: Repository methods return LeaveRequest/LeaveBalance and accept CreateLeaveRequestDto/UpdateLeaveRequestStatusDto; the types defined here are the contract for all data-access signatures.
The service orchestrates the LeaveRequest lifecycle using LeaveRequestStatus for state-machine guards and consumes the DTOs for apply/approve/reject/cancel operations.
The policy repository returns LeavePolicy objects and uses the LeaveType union for findByLeaveType lookups.
The type unions must stay in lockstep with the database CHECK constraints so that values valid in TypeScript are also valid at the persistence layer.
